title: Aromatic Japanese Rice Tan Tan Udon
description: A comforting Kyushu noodle dish that blends fragrant cloves, fried ground rice, and a savory broth into a crunchy, herbal udon bowl, perfect for a halal-friendly meal.
instructions: Bring dashi broth, water, soy sauce, mirin, and sesame oil to a gentle simmer in a medium pot.
Add ground cloves, grated ginger, and sliced shiitake mushrooms and simmer for 3 minutes to infuse the flavors.
Stir in fried ground rice and shredded cabbage, cooking until the cabbage is tender, about 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a separate pan and lightly toast the dry udon noodles in a dry skillet until golden and fragrant, then break them into smaller pieces.
Add the toasted udon noodles to the simmering broth, letting them cook for 4 minutes until al dente.
Taste the broth and adjust seasoning with extra soy sauce if needed.
Remove the pot from heat, ladle the noodles and broth into bowls, and garnish with chopped scallions and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve hot, optionally adding a boiled egg on the side for extra protein.
